name: A Product Completion Cannot Produce Two Eligible Failing Rows
statement: Let $0\in P\subseteq T$ both peel to $0$, and let positive ample $R$ have unique corner $0$ but fail to peel to $0$. Put $C=P\vee R$, $D_0=P\times R$, and $D_1=T\vee R$, with both factors nontrivial. Then $D_0$ never peels to $C$, but the crossed contraction $K=(D_1,D_0)$ is dismantlable ample exactly when $T$ peels to $P$, exactly when $D_1$ peels to $C$. Thus this product-completion template cannot have a positive contraction while both enlarged rows fail relatively.
proof: Product corners satisfy $\operatorname{Cor}(D_0)=\operatorname{Cor}(P)\times\{0\}\subseteq C$, excluding a first relative deletion. Express $K$ as the relative attachment of $R$ to two peripheral families $L\subseteq B$. The exact attachment test makes $K$ positive precisely when $B$ peels to $L$. Projecting any such chain gives $T\searrow P$; conversely, a relative order $T\searrow P$ followed by $P\searrow\{0\}$ lifts to $B\searrow L$. Restriction to the zero face of $R$ and the reverse lifted construction show $D_1\searrow C$ is equivalent to the same condition.
